prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor ground plane receding from beneath the camera wearer out to several metres, with one helmeted cyclist standing directly in front of the wearer and a bicycle positioned to the lower right. In frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer's extended left and right arms are brightest at 0.3 to 0.6 m, reaching forward to touch the upper back of the cyclist (whose torso and helmeted head sit at roughly 0.6 to 0.9 m and face away from the wearer), while the bicycle handlebars and frame sit 0.3 to 0.5 m to the right of the cyclist at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 m from the wearer. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer's right arm drops out of view while the left arm remains extended toward the cyclist's left shoulder, and the cyclist retreats slightly to about 1.0 to 1.3 m, exposing more of the bicycle's saddle, frame, and handlebars below and to the right within both individuals' arm's reach. Compared to the dark nighttime RGB frames, the depth map much more clearly reveals the continuous slope of the ground plane and the full silhouette of the dark shirt, limbs, and bicycle frame against the background. However, the map is unreliable around the bright red LED clip light on the cyclist's back (which causes local depth bleeding that merges the wearer's hands with the cyclist's back in frames 1 to 4) and completely loses the distant illuminated building (>15 m away) into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the foreground human silhouettes and the bicycle in the lower right against an unlabelled black background, where the cyclist stands directly in front of the camera wearer at 0.6 to 1.3 m facing away and never looking back. Within arm's reach (under 0.8 m), the camera wearer's own outstretched arms enter from the bottom left and bottom right to contact the back of the cyclist's shoulders, partially occluding the cyclist's upper back in frames 1 to 3 before the right arm withdraws in frame 4 and the cyclist steps slightly forward by frame 5. In frame 5, as the cyclist moves further ahead and slightly left relative to the bicycle (about 0.3 m apart), two overlapping 'bicycle' masks (yellow and orange) finally appear in the lower right at 1.0 to 1.5 m, sitting below the cyclist's right arm which is raised to his helmet within his own reach. The segmentation map makes the outer contour of the dark-clothed figures and the frame-5 bicycle handlebars and seat much easier to distinguish from the dark pavement and shadows than in the low-light RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable in separating touching people and objects: in frame 1 it splits the cyclist's head and the merged torso/wearer-arms into two separate 'person' instances, in frames 2 to 5 it fuses the camera wearer's arms and the cyclist into a single pink 'person' mask with a small unsegmented hole where the red light sits, and in frames 1 to 4 it completely fails to detect the partially visible bicycle in the bottom-right corner.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a single yellow body skeleton for the cyclist standing 0.6 to 1.3 m directly in front of the camera wearer, showing shoulder and hip joints as a trapezoid in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 while omitting the lower legs, which are out of the bottom of the frame. Across all five frames, the cyclist faces away from the camera wearer—with his torso narrowing in frame 4 as he turns slightly and shrinking in frame 5 as he moves about 0.4 m further forward—and in frame 5 his right elbow bends upward to place his right hand (the only detected magenta hand skeleton) at the right side of his helmeted head, well within his own reach. While the RGB image shows the camera wearer's two arms reaching within 0.5 m in front of the lens to hold a small red light against the cyclist's upper back, the pose map detects neither the wearer's limbs nor the nearby bicycle to the lower right. The skeleton map helps clarify the orientation of the cyclist's dark-clothed torso, hip line, and raised right arm posture in frame 5, which nearly blend into the dark background and shadows in the RGB strip. However, the map is unreliable in several ways: it completely misses the camera wearer's foreground arms and hands in all five frames, fails to detect the cyclist's hips in frame 3 and left arm in frame 4, and hallucinates clusters of facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) on the back of the cyclist's helmet and neck even though he is facing away from the camera.
